before.workflow: Actual archived worker post-restore statements; original files restored in fixture; SCM stubbed.
before.failure: Worker preserved the obsolete wrapper: EgoistShieldSystemDoH

checks: PASS: actual worker restore sequence migrates three exact stopped aliases and records rollback state
PASS: verified aliases are idempotent and stopped intent is preserved
PASS: a running third service prevents every replacement
PASS: changed current SCM ownership prevents every replacement
PASS: a CIM query failure prevents every replacement
PASS: changed saved registration prevents every replacement
PASS: a substituted manifest hash cannot approve arbitrary code
PASS: corrupt packaged source prevents every replacement
PASS: a stale installed manifest prevents every replacement
PASS: altered original backup prevents every replacement
PASS: an unknown current binary prevents every replacement
PASS: duplicate service ownership records are refused
PASS: locked second alias fails atomically; recovery stops three owned aliases and restores originals
PASS: an unstarted wrapper migration causes no service stop
PASS: recovery rejects a substituted SCM registration
PASS: recovery propagates a CIM lookup failure without stopping an unverified service
PASS: migration refuses a real junction before reading or writing outside paths
PASS: an outside destination is rejected
PASS: missing or older framework fails; exact 4.8 threshold and 4.8.1 pass
PASS: actual worker refuses unsupported framework before every backup and stop
PASS: actual worker snapshot failure does not stop Core or invoke recovery

existingRuntimeXml.engineConfigurationValidation: Real Xray run -test under isolated fixture

checks: PASS: a pre-handoff failure does not stop services or launch the desktop
PASS: legacy state without the handoff marker still runs recovery
PASS: recovery does not claim payload rollback or start the desktop while its marker remains pending

limits: No live SCM, registry, adapter, DNS or installed-app mutation.
Actual services, driver loading, reboot and prolonged runtime require separate production acceptance.
WinSW status/version confirms Framework launch and alias/XML compatibility; it does not prove child-engine start or recovery.
